assembly.readWith: ilspycmd 11.0.0.9375, read-only type and member listing
assembly.note: The generated interop assemblies are Il2CppInterop runtime-invoke thunks; they carry the member set, the virtual slot and the field offset, but no game logic. A native field is exposed as a property of the field's own name, which is what `ForgeWeapon/tests/AttackInstance/NativeMemberTests.cs` reads through Mono.Cecil.

reusedFor: The four Fire bodies are the complete per-shot hook set and no Fire body reaches another (w4-player-fire).
A player's every ranged hit reaches BulletWeapon.BulletHit inside the Fire body, so the scope can answer the miss question when that body returns (w4-player-fire `hit-routine`).
The synced pair runs for a non-local player's weapon on this machine, which is why a client's attack is observed on the host (w4-player-fire `syncChain`).

answer.question: Which native members carry the attack-instance facts of this build, and is the accepted/missed rule observable at all?
conclusion: A ranged attack's whole lifecycle is one Fire body. The request is the body's own entry (`Fire(System.Boolean)`, one optional bool), the close is its return, and every hit the attack causes is resolved inside it: `BulletWeapon.BulletHit` is reached from the four Fire bodies and from the sentry's own firing component, and the shotgun's two hit sites sit inside its pellet loop.

The native acceptance signal is `PlayerSync.RegisterFiredBullets(int)`: its complete literal caller set in this build is `Gear.BulletWeapon::Fire` and `Gear.Shotgun::Fire`. A pull the weapon refused never calls it, which is what makes 'the shot counter of the equipment life moved inside the body' the acceptance test rather than a Forge guess.

Melee has no Fire. `Gear.MeleeWeaponFirstPerson.DoTriggerAttack(System.Boolean)` is the attack entry and `OnAttackHitDone()` is the end of the swing; the state enum `Gear.eMeleeWeaponState` declares the twelve attack states, so the melee half is anchored on declared types.

The game's own empty-clip path is an explicit member: `Gear.BWA_Burst.OnFireShotEmptyClip()` and `Gear.BWA_Auto.OnFireShotEmptyClip()`. The dry-fire fact is published from that decision and never from comparing a clip readback against zero.

A burst sequence has two declared ends on the two burst-capable archetypes: `BWA_Burst` and `BWA_Auto` each declare `OnStartFiring()` and `OnStopFiring()`. `BWA_SemiBurst` derives from `BWA_Semi` and declares neither an end nor an empty-clip path, so it carries no sequence hook.
The burst length the `burst_*` facts carry is `Gear.BulletWeapon.m_burstMax`, a native int on the weapon itself, not a Forge tally.
A weapon's attack scope is named `gtfo.weapon.attack:<equipment life>:<n>`, one sequence per equipment life, the same identity scheme ruling 78 gave the shot scope.

`forge.trigger.combat.attack_cancelled` has no native signal. Nothing in the four Fire bodies, in `MeleeWeaponFirstPerson` or in `PlayerInventoryBase` reports an interrupted trigger pull, and the design's `reason` was to be a native reason code; there is none to read.

hostVisibility.authority: Every fact here is published on the host only, through the same gate the shot and hit facts use: SNet.IsMaster, the host's ready lifecycle and the equipment life's owner resolving to a current gtfo.player reference.
hostVisibility.syncedBodies: The two synced Fire bodies run on this machine for another player's weapon, so the host observes a client's attack there; the unsynced bodies are the firing player's own.
hostVisibility.melee: The melee weapon runs only on the machine whose player swings it, so a client's swing is not observed on the host by this hook set.
unverified: Nothing here was executed. The facts above are static: the member set, the call edges w4-player-fire.json proved, and the interop metadata.

That BWA_SemiBurst's inherited OnStartFiring/OnStopFiring are not reached, and that its empty clip leaves no native trace, is read from the metadata (it declares neither member). A runtime trace of a semi-burst weapon would settle it.
That the empty-clip members really run on every dry pull, rather than only on some archetypes' paths, is a runtime fact this metadata cannot show.

integration.declarations: The eight row documents live in ForgeWeapon/AttackInstanceContract.cs verbatim from catalog/capability-catalog.json; the integration batch moves them into ForgeRuntime/Framework/TriggerContracts.cs, because every forge.trigger.* row is declared once by forge.contract.trigger and a second declaration of one id is refused at registration.
integration.bindings: Seven observe bindings, one per implemented row, are spelled in the same file and registered by ForgeWeapon/ModuleDefinition.cs's capability and binding lists; the cancelled row carries no binding and its absence is recorded in AttackInstanceContract.Gaps.
nativeHalves: ForgeWeapon/Native/AttackInstanceHooks.cs is a new Compile item in ForgeWeapon/Native/ForgeWeapon.Native.csproj and its sixteen hook classes are added to WeaponNativeHooks.Types.
The session builds the module in WeaponNativeSession.Start and exposes it as WeaponNativeSession.Attack.
EquipmentNativeAdapter implements IAttackNativeReads and counts hit candidates per equipment life in its own PublishEvent.
integration.releaseManifest: No row is added by hand: the eight declarations and the seven bindings enter Release/export-runtime-manifest's output only after the integration batch registers them, exactly like the a-wpn slice's six action rows.
integration.nativeLayout: No new native read or write is registered by the module: it reads the equipment life's own counters through the adapter, and the four weapon members it names (m_burstMax, m_burstCurrentCount, m_weapon, and the two melee callbacks) are checked against the interop metadata by this slice's own NativeMemberTests.
